VitaNova Pharmaceuticals - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaNova Pharmaceuticals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaNova Pharmaceuticals' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO of VitaNova Pharmaceuticals.

Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. VitaNova delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust demand across our oncology franchise, particularly our PD-1 inhibitor VitaPD1, which solidified its leadership position following label expansions, and continued uptake of our CAR-T therapy VitaCell-T in hematologic malignancies. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including geographic expansion, lifecycle management of our blockbusters, upcoming catalysts, and value-creating business development.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives. First, on geographic revenue breakdown and emerging market growth, we're seeing accelerating contributions from high-growth regions that are outpacing our core markets. Then, we'll address our patent cliff exposure and the comprehensive lifecycle management strategies we've implemented to mitigate risks and extend value. I'll also touch on revenue guidance and key upcoming catalysts that position us for accelerated growth. Finally, our business development efforts in licensing, acquisitions, and partnerships are delivering meaningful non-dilutive capital and pipeline enhancements.

We are particularly excited about VitaPD1 and its potential to drive sustained leadership in immuno-oncology through new indications and combinations.

Now, I will turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Thank you, Michael. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $1.325 billion, an increase of 18% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by our oncology franchise—led by VitaPD1, now the market leader in the US following its label expansion into triple-negative breast cancer—and robust demand for VitaCell-T, along with $45 million in royalty and milestone revenues.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $1.42 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $410 million, or $2.05 per share.

Our operating expenses were $725 million, reflecting continued investment in R&D to advance our pipeline, offset by operational efficiencies in manufacturing and gross-to-net adjustments. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to support our pipeline, with our cash position remaining strong at $2.8 billion.

Before we open the floor to questions, let me dive deeper into our geographic revenue breakdown and the exciting momentum in emerging markets, a key growth driver as we execute our global expansion strategy.

For the quarter, we reported total net product revenues of $1.28 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter. Turning to geography, our revenue mix reflects maturity in established markets and accelerating contributions from emerging regions. North America accounted for 56% of total revenues, or $742 million, up 14% year-over-year. The US remains our powerhouse at $682 million, fueled by VitaPD1's 22% volume increase post-NRAS-mutant melanoma approval by the FDA in late Q2, with over 85% commercial coverage now in place. Canada contributed a steady $60 million, driven by uptake in our rare disease portfolio, including enzyme replacement therapy VitaZyme for Fabry disease.

Europe delivered 24% of revenues, or $318 million, growing 12% year-over-year despite volume-based procurement headwinds in Germany and Italy. Key wins included reimbursement for VitaCell-T in the UK's NHS Innovative Medicines Fund, driving a 30% sequential ramp, and strong performance in France and Spain where VitaPD1 captured 15% market share in first-line NSCLC per IQVIA data. Our EU pricing strategy, averaging 45% of US list prices, supports access while preserving margins.

Asia-Pacific surged to 12% of revenues, or $159 million, up 42% year-over-year, our fastest-growing region. Japan and Australia each contributed around $40 million, with Japan tenders for VitaPD1 biosimilar competitors offset by premium pricing on VitaCell-T, which received orphan drug designation extension. China grew 58% to $65 million, thanks to our partnership with Sinopharm for local commercialization, initiating over 25,000 patients on VitaPD1 through NRDL inclusion at a 70% discount to US WAC, similar to the Keytruda model.

Latin America represented 5%, or $66 million, up 28% year-over-year, led by Brazil at $32 million where ANVISA approval for VitaZyme unlocked $100 million in tenders over the next 12 months. Mexico and Argentina added $20 million and $14 million, respectively, bolstered by direct-to-patient access programs despite currency volatility.

Other emerging markets, including India, the Middle East, and Africa, rounded out at 3%, or $40 million, with 35% growth driven by Cipla's distribution of our biosimilar insulin glargine portfolio in India, capturing 12% share in the GLP-1 combo space amid the diabetes epidemic.

Emerging markets as a whole—Asia-Pacific ex-Japan/Australia, Latin America, and other EM—now comprise 20% of total revenues, up from 14% a year ago and 16% in Q2. This $265 million grew 39% year-over-year, outpacing company growth by more than 2x; ex-FX, it's 44%, underscoring our volume-led strategy.

Strategic initiatives propelling this include regulatory milestones like NRDL reimbursement in China for VitaCell-T, positioning it against Kymriah with a 20% cost advantage and local manufacturing at our Suzhou facility at 60% capacity. In India, CDSCO approval for our next-gen bispecific VitaBispec targets the $2.5 billion RA market, launching H1 2025 via our 50/50 JV with Dr. Reddy's.

We've invested $250 million in our Brazil API plant and Singapore hub for ASEAN, reducing lead times by 40% and expanding EM gross margins to 72% from 68% globally. Our VitaAccess initiative has enrolled 50,000 EM patients year-to-date, offering named-patient programs for VitaPD1 at cost-plus-10%, driving 50% uptake in Brazil's low-income segments.

Pipeline tailwinds include three Phase 3 trials with EM-specific readouts, like ADCs for HER2-low breast cancer in India/China and CRISPR gene editing for sickle cell in Brazil.

Looking ahead, EM should contribute 23-25% of FY2025 revenues with mid-30% growth, supported by $300 million in tenders. We've hedged 70% of 2024 FX exposures, and our biosimilar pipeline—five launches by 2026, including Humira equivalent—positions us in the $100 billion market.

This diversification de-risks our base and aligns with our mission to democratize precision medicine.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to $2.65 billion to $2.75 billion in revenue, representing 18% to 23% growth at the midpoint, up from prior $2.4 billion to $2.6 billion. This reflects stronger Q3 performance and demand across oncology (68% of revenue, $1.8-1.9 billion) and immunology/rare diseases (32%, $850-900 million). US at 72% ($1.9-2.0 billion), Europe 18% ($475-525 million), ex-US international 10% growing 35%.

Headwinds include $50 million from 340B rebates and $30 million Medicaid adjustments, offset by COGS at 22% from yield optimizations and API reductions.

Key catalysts include Q4 Phase 3 topline for VitaPD1 in HCC mid-October, targeting 35% PFS improvement and $750 million US peak; FDA PDUFA November 15 for VitaCell-T earlier-line myeloma, doubling patients to 25,000; late Q4 Roche partnership for T-cell engager with $400 million upfront; and Q4 manufacturing milestones like Leiden continuous line for 30% COGS reduction.

We're guiding 2025 revenue to $3.4-3.7 billion, with OpEx at $1.75 billion, R&D 28% of revenues.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:
Thank you, Elena. Before we open for questions, let me address our patent cliff exposure and lifecycle management strategies, critical to long-term value. Our flagship VitaPD1, generating $4.2 billion last year or 45% of revenue, faces primary patent expiry in H2 2027 in US/EU. Without action, we'd see 75-85% erosion from biosimilars via BPCIA.

But our proactive LCM has de-risked this. First, VitaPD1 XR subcutaneous formulation, FDA-approved Q1 2024 via 505(b)(2), reduces dosing to monthly SC, improving compliance 35% in COMFORT-2 (n=1,248), ramping to $450 million US run-rate at 25% share. EU approved May, shielding 20% sales through 2032.

Second, label expansions: TNBC US Feb 2024, MSI-high endometrial EU Apr, adjuvant melanoma global, adding $1.1 billion peak, with TNBC driving 12% Q3 growth. Orphan designations add 7 years exclusivity.

Third, next-gen bridges: VitaPD1-2 bispecific PD-1/CTLA-4 in Phase III frontline NSCLC, $3.8 billion peak by 2030; VitaSynk combo with KRAS inhibitor K-RasBlock, Breakthrough Designation, 48% ORR vs 32%, for $50 billion KRAS market.

Regionally: US (65%) navigates IRA via SC pass-through, 85% assistance; EU (25%) offsets German AMNOG cuts with Eastern growth; EM (10%) surges 40% in China via Fosun.

Quantitatively, LCM flattens the cliff to 35-40% dip, with $1.2 billion from XR/extensions, $2.1 billion from next-gen, $800 million from divestitures, sustaining mid-teens EPS.

We're climbing the next peak in immuno-oncology.

Our business development also bolsters this. In Q3, $178 million BD revenue, 22% of total, up 45% YoY from milestones/upfronts.

Licensing: Global deal for ADC VitaADC-247 to Merck, $250 million upfront, $1.2 billion milestones, 18-22% royalties; ex-US ours for Asia HER2 market. In-licensed CRISPR-Cas13 from Broad spinout, $45 million + $300 million biobucks for autoimmune.

Acquisitions: $620 million GeneX for Phase 1 AAV ophthalmology therapies, accretive with $120 million milestones, $35 million synergies.

Partnerships: Pfizer opt-in $100 million for bispecific BPI-BiTE-89, 70% cost share, 50/50 ex-US; Novartis ex-China for VEGF trap; WuXi/CSPC for obesity GLP-1RA in China, $2.5 billion peak.

US milestones $300 million YTD; Europe EMA Q1 2025; Asia enrollment 85%. $800 million milestones next 12 months, two Alzheimer's term sheets.

These position our $15 billion pipeline as a serial monetizer.

We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Elena, on the emerging markets growth to 20% of revenue, can you elaborate on the risks like FX and pricing reforms in India, and how the biosimilar launches factor into FY2025?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Thanks, David. FX volatility is a noted risk—we've hedged 70% of 2024 exposures. India's PPAC reforms add pricing pressure, but our volume-led strategy and five biosimilar launches by 2026, including Humira equivalent, target the $100 billion market for share gains. EM growth to 23-25% in FY2025 with mid-30% rates remains on track, supported by $300 million tenders and localized manufacturing.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. Michael, on the patent cliff for VitaPD1, how confident are you in the next-gen offsets like VitaPD1-2, and any update on regional tailoring?

Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:
Lisa, very confident—VitaPD1-2's Phase III in NSCLC forecasts $3.8 billion peak, offsetting 90% of the cliff with 60% margins. VitaSynk combo adds more. Regionally, US CMS pass-through for XR counters IRA; EU volume in East offsets pricing; China 40% surge via local production. Overall, 35-40% dip managed seamlessly.

Operator:
Our next question is from Mark Thompson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mark Thompson, Morgan Stanley:
Thanks. Elena, the raised guidance embeds conservative pricing—walk us through the HCC readout probability and Roche partnership details.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Mark, yes, conservative on pricing. HCC Phase 3 mid-October targets 35% PFS over standards, 65% POS per consensus, $750 million US peak, $300 million accelerated 2025 revenue. Roche term sheet for T-cell engager: $400 million upfront, $1.5 billion milestones, they handle ex-US, we keep US—de-risks $2 billion pipeline.

Operator:
Thank you. One more from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera, Barclays:
Quick one on BD—GeneX acquisition synergies and how it fits ophthalmology?

Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:
Alex, GeneX's AAVs with 10x efficiency expand our VEGF trap franchise ($89 million Q3 royalties). $35 million R&D savings via NC consolidation, $120 million milestones—immediate accretion, modular for CNS too.

Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the VitaNova Pharmaceuticals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
